quarterly_data.signal: CSO Mike Quigley on clinical data: the 48-week phase II-B asthma study of lunsekimig (rendered 'lunsekimab' in the transcript) achieved statistically significant exacerbation and FEV1 endpoints in an all-comer population in which only 40% of patients had high eosinophils, with more meaningful improvement in the pre-specified subset with two or more exacerbations; Sanofi's modeling suggests significant improvement across all three registrational endpoints in a phase III, and he cited PRO improvements over standard of care. For the AATD asset efdoralprin alfa (rendered 'duvakitug alfa'), the Q3-week regimen hit all primary and secondary endpoints versus the Q4-week regimen and plasma-derived AAT; the regulatory gating factor is the correlation between biomarkers and clinical outcome, not safety, with no significant permanent discontinuations based on adverse events and some transient anti-drug antibodies (transcript: 'only two were found to be non-neutralizing in two patients'). In VITALIZE, 70% of IVIG-dependent CIDP patients progress upon withdrawal, and the IDMC stopped MOBILIZE on futility with no safety findings. The TNF/OX40L bispecific (rendered 'revekimab') phase II-B in hidradenitis suppurativa next year will decide the move to phase III, judged on HS scores and tunnels. The PD-1/IL-15 asset is in phase II in colorectal and lung cancer, with colorectal data stratified with and without liver metastases; the geographic atrophy gene therapy targets two key nodes of the complement pathway.
